editorialPlan.title: Why node-pty still fails after rebuild
editorialPlan.objective: Explain why a successful npm rebuild message does not prove that a native module can be loaded, then show a verifiable repair.

audience.description: Node.js maintainers who understand npm and CI but do not routinely debug native addons.
priorKnowledge: CI runs commands in a clean environment
likelyMisconceptions: A zero rebuild exit code guarantees that pty.node exists
Re-running the same rebuild command is a sufficient verification

editorialPlan.thesis: The rebuild command can succeed while npm blocks the install script that produces pty.node, so verification must test both the artifact and the import.

patterns.reason: The source contains an observed failure, an expected install path, a break point, a root cause, and a verifiable repair.
adaptations: Combine repair and verification into the final section to stay within the duration budget.

patterns.reason: The conclusion must be supported by checking the native artifact and importing the module, not by trusting the rebuild message.

concepts.claim: Command success and native artifact existence are different conditions.
concepts.reason: This corrects the misconception exposed by the CI log.

concepts.claim: node-pty needs its install script to produce a platform-specific pty.node binary.
concepts.reason: The viewer needs a causal model before seeing the blocked step.

concepts.claim: allowScripts blocked the install step, leaving no loadable binary.
concepts.reason: This is the direct cause supported by the npm warning.

concepts.claim: Allow the required script, rebuild, and verify with an actual import.
concepts.reason: The repair is incomplete without executable verification.

concepts.claim: Review the complete history of Node ABI versions.
concepts.reason: It does not help diagnose the observed blocked-script failure.

sections.title: The misleading success signal
sections.expectedOutcome: The viewer stops treating the rebuild message as proof of loadability.

sections.title: What must happen during install
sections.expectedOutcome: The viewer can name the step that creates pty.node.

sections.title: Where the path was blocked
sections.expectedOutcome: The viewer connects the allowScripts warning to the missing binary.

sections.title: Repair and verify
sections.expectedOutcome: The viewer verifies the fix with an import rather than another success message.

visualDesignBrief.title: Native module causal trace
visualDesignBrief.direction: A quiet technical editorial treatment that keeps one causal statement active at a time and uses red only for the blocked install step.

palette.use: Blocked script and missing artifact only

layoutRules: Keep the title in the top safe area and the explanation in one central field.
Show no more than five diagram nodes at once.
Preserve left-to-right position across the install-path and root-cause scenes.
motionRules: Reveal one causal step per narration anchor.
Trace normal steps in blue and hold the blocked step in red for at least 1.5 seconds.
Use cuts within the causal sequence and a short fade before the repair.

sceneTreatments.composition: Place the success message above the missing-artifact statement with a not-equal sign between them.
sceneTreatments.emphasis: Reveal the missing artifact only when the narration says it is still absent.

sceneTreatments.composition: Use a left-to-right chain from package install to install script to build to pty.node.
sceneTreatments.emphasis: Trace the whole expected path in the normal accent color.

sceneTreatments.composition: Reuse the install path and isolate the allowScripts gate between install script and build.
sceneTreatments.emphasis: Only the blocked gate and missing pty.node use the failure color.

sceneTreatments.composition: Show the allowScripts configuration first, then the rebuild and import verification as a short code sequence.
sceneTreatments.emphasis: Finish on the import line, not the rebuild output.

avoid: Browser chrome without a real capture
